chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a woman who makes her female slave girl's private part permissible for her husband. He said, 'I dislike this; what will she do if she becomes pregnant?' I said, 'She will say, if she becomes pregnant from you, then she is for you.' He said, 'There is no harm in this.' I said, 'And a man does this with his brother?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.تُحِلُّ فَرْجَ: makes permissible the private part (for sexual access)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia juristic ruling on a husband having sexual relations with his wife's female slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the juristic permissibility of a woman granting her husband sexual access to her female slave, expressing initial dislike (*karah*) due to the risk of paternity disputes if she becomes pregnant. He resolves this by accepting the condition that the husband assumes responsibility for the child, thereby establishing a clear lineage, and extends this permissibility to a man granting his brother similar access. This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the flexibility of marital rights over slaves, prioritizing the resolution of lineage (*nasab*) through conditional agreement.
